title: Enhanced transpose of the unit and counit mate word
statement:
Use the enriched infinity categories and enhanced functor categories of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], with mapping objects in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$ and all required universes enlarged. An enhanced adjunction $L:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:R$ means enhanced functors with a natural equivalence of mapping objects $\mathcal D(LX,Y)\simeq\mathcal C(X,RY)$, with enhanced unit and counit and coherent triangle identities. For enhanced adjunctions $L_i:\mathcal C_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal D_i:R_i$ ($i=1,2$) with units $\eta_i$ and counits $\epsilon_i$, enhanced functors $G:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$ and $H:\mathcal D_1\to\mathcal D_2$, and an enhanced transformation $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$, form the mate word with the directions of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], with composition read right to left:
$$\beta=(R_2H\epsilon_1)(R_2\alpha R_1)(\eta_2GR_1):GR_1\to R_2H.$$
Its transpose under $L_2\dashv R_2$ is $(H\epsilon_1)(\alpha R_1):L_2GR_1\to H$. More precisely, the induced transposition is an equivalence between the full enhanced transformation objects $\operatorname{Nat}(GR_1,R_2H)$ and $\operatorname{Nat}(L_2GR_1,H)$, carrying $\beta$ to that composite. This equivalence and its specified comparison commute with restriction of parameter diagrams, including their simplices and coherent homotopies.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, specified adjunction mates: the enhanced mate word and its transpose calculation. This is an agent-formulated foundation; no Stacks tag states the enhanced assertion.

proof.text:
Put $P=GR_1$, $Q=H$, $L=L_2$, $R=R_2$, $\eta=\eta_2$ and $\epsilon=\epsilon_2$. Work in the enhanced functor categories $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal D_1,\mathcal C_2)$ and $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal D_1,\mathcal D_2)$, where $\mathcal V=\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$. The coherent composition, evaluation and currying in [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] give postcomposition by $L,R$, the whiskered transformations $\eta P$ and $\epsilon Q$, and morphisms of mapping objects
$$T:\mathcal E(P,RQ)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(LP,Q),\quad b\longmapsto(\epsilon Q)(Lb),$$
$$S:\mathcal F(LP,Q)\longrightarrow\mathcal E(P,RQ),\quad a\longmapsto(Ra)(\eta P).$$
Here the formulas denote composites of enriched mapping-object morphisms, using the points representing $\eta P$ and $\epsilon Q$ in enriched composition. They therefore act on the whole derived objects, including generalized inputs from any object of $\mathcal V$, rather than only on degree-zero morphism classes. All these categories and inputs fit in the enlarged universes of the hypothesis.

source.place: Agent proof of enhanced mate transpose, step 1; expands the specified adjunction-mate calculation underlying proof paragraph 2.

proof.text:
Compute the composite on the entire object $\mathcal F(LP,Q)$ using the coherent composition of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus]:
$$TS(a)=(\epsilon Q)(LRa)(L\eta P)\simeq a(\epsilon LP)(L\eta P)\simeq a.$$
The first homotopy is the enriched naturality homotopy of the given counit, with variable input $a:LP\to Q$; it holds as a homotopy of mapping-object morphisms. The second is the given coherent triangle $(\epsilon L)(L\eta)\simeq\operatorname{id}_L$, whiskered by $P$ and then composed with $a$. Thus this is a homotopy $TS\simeq\operatorname{id}$ of morphisms in $\mathcal V$. No assertion that equality of object components alone detects such a homotopy is used.

source.place: Agent proof of enhanced mate transpose, step 2; expands the specified adjunction-mate calculation underlying proof paragraph 2.

proof.text:
On $\mathcal E(P,RQ)$ the other composite is
$$ST(b)=(R\epsilon Q)(RLb)(\eta P)\simeq(R\epsilon Q)(\eta RQ)b\simeq b.$$
Use enriched naturality of the given unit for the variable input $b:P\to RQ$, followed by the given triangle $(R\epsilon)(\eta R)\simeq\operatorname{id}_R$. Coherent composition in [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] lets us whisker and compose these homotopies as homotopies of morphisms of mapping objects. Hence $ST\simeq\operatorname{id}$. Together with step 2, $T,S$ are inverse equivalences of the full enhanced transformation objects. These are precisely the counit and unit transposition formulas of the specified enhanced adjunction.

source.place: Agent proof of enhanced mate transpose, step 3; expands the specified adjunction-mate calculation underlying proof paragraph 2.

proof.text:
Set $c=(H\epsilon_1)(\alpha R_1):LP\to Q$. By functoriality of $R_2$, the displayed word for the mate is
$$\beta=(R_2H\epsilon_1)(R_2\alpha R_1)(\eta_2GR_1)\simeq R_2(c)(\eta_2P)=S(c).$$
The order and domains are exactly those in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; this reference fixes the mate convention, and its ordinary bijection is not being invoked for enhanced objects. The coherent composition and functoriality of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] give the displayed identification. Apply the homotopy $TS\simeq\operatorname{id}$ from step 2 to $c$. It supplies the specified comparison
$$T(\beta)\simeq c=(H\epsilon_1)(\alpha R_1),$$
with source $L_2GR_1$ and target $H$, as required.

source.place: Agent proof of enhanced mate transpose, step 4; expands the specified adjunction-mate calculation underlying proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: For a parameter shape $K$, form the same operations with $K$-diagrams of the given data, units, counits and triangle homotopies. By [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus], cotensors retain coherent natural transformations and satisfy $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B^K)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)^K$; composition, evaluation and currying are coherent. For a map of parameter shapes $u:J\to K$, evaluation of a diagram on $u$ sends each composite in $T,S$ to the same composite of the restricted inputs: in particular $u^*((\epsilon Q)(Lb))\simeq(u^*\epsilon\,u^*Q)((u^*L)(u^*b))$, and the analogous formula holds for $S$. It also restricts the naturality homotopies and the two given triangle homotopies used in steps 2 and 3. Restricting the identity $\beta\simeq S(c)$ and its $TS$ homotopy therefore gives precisely step 4 for the restricted data. Taking $K=\Delta^n$ and $u$ a face or degeneracy shows that these comparisons include the simplices and their homotopies, with their compatibility under successive restrictions furnished by the same coherent evaluation. No choices of inverses or componentwise homotopies are made after restricting.
